subject: ss-neurology
title: Coma, Encephalopathy and Brain Death Determination

steps.tx: **Coma** represents a profound state of unarousable, sustained unresponsiveness in which a patient exhibits complete absence of awareness and purposeful behavioural interaction with the surrounding environment. Neuroanatomically, maintaining normal wakefulness and alertness requires an intact, functioning **reticular activating system** located within the rostral brainstem tegmentum projecting diffusely to bilateral cerebral hemispheres. Structural brainstem destruction or widespread bilateral cerebral cortical failure represents the physiological substrate of comatose states.
steps.say: Coma is defined as a profound state of unarousable unresponsiveness lacking purposeful behavioural responses to internal or external stimuli. Normal wakefulness relies upon the ascending reticular activating system within the brainstem projecting diffusely to both cerebral hemispheres. Coma arises from structural lesions damaging the rostral brainstem tegmentum or extensive bilateral hemispheric dysfunction.

steps.tx: Standardized clinical bedside evaluation of acute conscious impairment employs structured behavioral scoring systems. The **Glasgow Coma Scale** objectively quantifies **impairment of consciousness** by evaluating Eye (**1-4**), Verbal (**1-5**), and Motor (**1-6**) responses, yielding scores ranging from 3 to 15. An aggregate score of 8 or lower formally designates severe coma requiring emergency endotracheal airway protection to prevent aspiration.
steps.say: The Glasgow Coma Scale provides an objective bedside assessment of consciousness impairment. It quantifies eye opening from one to four, verbal response from one to five, and motor response from one to six. Total scores range from three to fifteen, with scores of eight or less defining severe coma.

steps.tx: Stereotyped posturing patterns furnish critical neuroanatomical localization in deeply comatose patients. **Decorticate posturing** manifests with rigid flexion and adduction of the upper extremities alongside extension and internal rotation of the lower limbs. This stereotypic posture indicates severe bilateral cortical or diencephalic injury occurring above the level of the midbrain, with anatomical preservation of the **red nucleus** and rubrospinal tracts producing disinhibited upper limb flexion.
steps.say: Decorticate posturing indicates severe structural or metabolic dysfunction above the midbrain with anatomic preservation of the red nucleus. Patients have rigid flexion of the upper limbs and extension of the lower limbs. Disinhibited rubrospinal tract activity drives upper extremity flexion while corticospinal interruption produces lower limb extensor posturing.

left.title: Decorticate Posturing (Flexor)
points: Upper limb flexion and adduction with lower limb extension
Lesion level above midbrain (cortex or diencephalon)
Red nucleus and rubrospinal tract functionally preserved

right.title: Decerebrate Posturing (Extensor)
points: Upper limb extension and pronation with lower limb extension
Lesion level between red nucleus and vestibular nuclei
Unchecked vestibulospinal excitation carries poorer prognosis

steps.tx: Caudal progression of brainstem compression produces severe extensor motor patterns. **Decerebrate posturing** exhibits rigid extension, adduction, and pronation of the arms accompanied by rigid **extensor posturing** of both legs with plantar flexion. This posturing pattern reflects destructive lesions affecting the midbrain and upper pons below the red nucleus, allowing unchecked excitatory output from intact lateral vestibulospinal tracts to dominate motor pathways, portending a worse prognosis.
steps.say: Decerebrate posturing reflects damage situated between the red nucleus in the midbrain and the vestibular nuclei in the lower pons. Patients present with rigid extension, adduction, and pronation of the upper extremities alongside lower limb extension. Unchecked activity from lateral vestibulospinal pathways drives this extensor posture and portends worse clinical outcomes.

steps.tx: Preconditions for **brain death** determination require establishing an irreversible proximate cause while ruling out confounders. Core body **temperature** must be maintained above 36 degrees Celsius, and systolic blood pressure maintained above 100 mmHg. Clinicians must meticulously exclude central nervous system depressant medications, therapeutic neuromuscular blockade, and severe uncorrected metabolic disturbances before testing.
steps.say: Pupillary light responses serve as an indispensable localizing sign in acute coma evaluations. An expanding uncal mass directly compresses the third cranial nerve, producing an ipsilateral fixed dilated pupil. Bilateral pinpoint reactive pupils indicate pontine hemorrhage or opioid toxicity, whereas bilateral fixed dilated pupils denote irreversible midbrain damage or brain death.

rows: Severe midbrain ischemia or uncal herniation

steps.tx: Comprehensive clinical testing confirms the complete absence of all **brainstem reflexes**. Testing verifies absent pupillary light responses, absent corneal reflexes, absent oculocephalic doll-eye reflexes, absent **oculovestibular** cold calorics, and absent gag and cough reflexes. The formal apnea test provides physiological confirmation of absent medullary respiratory drive.
steps.say: Determining brain death requires proving irreversible cessation of all cerebral and brainstem activity. Before initiating testing, clinicians must confirm an irreversible etiology and exclude confounding factors. Core temperature must exceed thirty six degrees Celsius, systolic pressure must exceed one hundred millimeters of mercury, and all sedative drugs or paralytics must be fully cleared.

steps.tx: **Apnea testing** confirms brain death when pre-oxygenated patients demonstrate absent spontaneous breathing effort despite arterial **PaCO2** rising to 60 mmHg or greater (or at least 20 mmHg above baseline) alongside an arterial pH below **7.28**. If profound hypotension or cardiac arrhythmia develops during testing, the patient must be immediately reconnected to mechanical ventilation.
steps.say: Apnea testing confirms brain death when pre oxygenated patients show absent spontaneous breathing despite arterial carbon dioxide rising to sixty millimeters of mercury or higher with an arterial pH below seven point two eight. If hemodynamic instability emerges, mechanical ventilation must be resumed immediately.

steps.tx: Ancillary confirmatory tests are indicated when apnea evaluation cannot be completed safely. Validated diagnostic modalities include four-vessel **cerebral angiography** demonstrating complete absence of intracranial arterial filling, and **transcranial Doppler** ultrasonography showing reverberating flow or systolic spikes. Radionuclide brain scintigraphy demonstrating the empty skull sign provides definitive corroboration.
steps.say: Ancillary confirmatory tests for brain death are indicated when clinical apnea testing cannot be completed. Four vessel cerebral angiography and transcranial Doppler ultrasound provide proof of intracranial circulatory arrest. Radionuclide perfusion imaging showing absent tracer uptake provides definitive corroboration.
